{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 places all three in the Cupredoxins superfamily, b.6.1 (sunid 49503), within the Cupredoxin-like fold, b.6 (49502), and All beta proteins class, b (48724). They belong to distinct families: Plastocyanin/azurin-like, b.6.1.1 (49504); Ephrin ectodomain, b.6.1.5 (74874); and Peptidylarginine deiminase Pad4, N-terminal domain, b.6.1.6 (110107).

Thus SCOPe recognizes probable common evolutionary ancestry at the superfamily level, despite their different biological roles. Family membership indicates a closer evolutionary relationship; a shared fold alone describes structural similarity without establishing homology, and class alone describes secondary-structure composition.

Copper binding or electron transfer should not be transferred across these families. Characterized plastocyanins and azurins are copper-dependent electron carriers, whereas ephrin ectodomains bind Eph receptors in cell signaling. PAD4 is a calcium-dependent peptidylarginine deiminase; its catalytic C-terminal domain is separately classified as d.126.1.5. Classification of its N-terminal domain as a cupredoxin does not establish copper binding, electron transfer, or localization of deiminase catalysis to that domain. Nor does the superfamily name guarantee copper binding in every member.

Functional transfer requires independent evidence: conservation and three-dimensional geometry of copper-coordinating residues, demonstrated copper occupancy/binding and appropriate spectroscopy, and—for electron transfer—redox measurements and activity with relevant partners. Sequence relationships, domain architecture, and physiological context also matter. A shared scaffold may support a structural template for the conserved core, but cannot by itself justify copying metal sites, receptor-binding surfaces, or function.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=cupredoxin","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49502","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ephrin&limit=5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=PAD4&limit=5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=plastocyanin&limit=5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/b.6.1.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/74874","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/110107","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/b.6.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/48724","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49504","Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy and protein functions"]}]}
